title: Salvaggio band personnel: Philip Salvaggio, Perkins, DeShari, Pudra
summary: Joe Salvaggio played piano, brother Philip led on alto and clarinet; tenor men George Perkins and Jack DeShari, and bass horn John Pudra.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: He's a very fine piano player. Very fine pianist. He still plays. He's around still playing. His brother played lead alto sax and clarinet. I don't know if the brothers playing sax and clarinet any more, but Joe, the leader of the group, was a very fine musician.
Do you remember his brother's name?

Yeah. Philip. Philip Salvaggio. And he was a very fine sax player. How many reads did he have in the band? We had three saxes. Three saxes. And we had trumpet and trombone and guitar, or banjo, and bass horn, and Joe on piano.
Who played tenor in the band?

Well, we went through two or three different tenor men. George Perkins, who's passed away since, the late George Perkins, who was a very fine tenor man. He was one of the tenor men. And at another time we had a boy by the name of Jack DeShari. He was a very fine tenor man. I think Jack has since passed away too.
And third alto? And third alto?

I don't recall who was on third alto. Like I say, Dick, we had several, during the four years we went through changes, you know. We probably had two or three different men on third alto also. I can't remember.

I think Jack DeShari played third alto, because George Perkins played tenor. And Philip played lead alto sax and clarinet. And on trumpet? And on bass horn we had a very fine audition by the name of John Pudra. I don't know if he's still in town or whether he's still around or what, but John Pudra was a very fine bass horn player.
There was a composer by that name, but I think he must have been older than that man.

Well, I would say John Pudra today would be in his around middle fifties, fifty-five, fifty-six, maybe fifty-eight, fifty-seven. Well, let's see. If he was still living. I think he must be, I think they moved out of town, I'm not sure. But John Pudra was a very fine bass player. Well you were playing... Bass horn player. Yeah.
